name: Bearded Fireworm
funFact: Has hollow, venom-filled bristles that cause intense burning pain on contact.

name: Blue Glaucus
funFact: Floats upside-down on the surface tension of the water, using stored air bubbles.

name: Spanish Dancer
funFact: Named for its spectacular undulating swimming motion that resembles a flamenco dancer.

name: Leaf Sheep
funFact: Is one of the only animals capable of photosynthesis, stealing chloroplasts from algae.

name: Sea Butterfly
funFact: Swims by flapping its wing-like shell extensions, resembling a butterfly in flight.

name: Sea Angel
funFact: Is a shell-less snail that swims with graceful wing-like movements.

name: California Sea Hare
funFact: Can release a cloud of purple ink when threatened, confusing predators.

name: Giant Clam
funFact: Can weigh over 500 pounds and live for more than 100 years.

name: Geoduck
funFact: Can live for over 160 years, making it one of the longest-living animals on Earth.

name: Atlantic Surf Clam
funFact: Can propel itself out of the sand using its muscular foot when disturbed.

name: Bay Scallop
funFact: Can swim short distances by rapidly clapping its shell valves together.

name: Blue Mussel
funFact: Attaches to rocks using strong byssal threads, forming dense beds of thousands.

name: Thorny Oyster
funFact: Shell is covered in long, sharp spines that deter predators.

name: Lion Paw Scallop
funFact: Named for its ridged, colorful shell that resembles a lion's paw.

name: Nautilus Pompilius
funFact: Shell follows a logarithmic spiral, one of nature's most perfect mathematical forms.

name: Paper Nautilus
funFact: Females create a delicate, paper-thin shell for egg protection.

name: Atlantic Horseshoe Crab
funFact: Has been virtually unchanged for 450 million years, predating the dinosaurs.

name: Japanese Horseshoe Crab
funFact: Its blue blood contains Limulus Amebocyte Lysate, used to test for bacterial contamination in medical equipment.

name: Indo-Pacific Horseshoe Crab
funFact: Is the only horseshoe crab species found in Asian coastal waters.

name: Sea Squirt
funFact: Is more closely related to vertebrates than most invertebrates, being a chordate.

name: Marine Flatworm
funFact: Can regenerate an entire organism from a fragment as small as 1/200th of its body.

name: Deep-Sea Pennatula
funFact: Produces bioluminescent waves that travel along its colony when physically disturbed.

name: Dodo
funFact: The dodo was a flightless bird from Mauritius that went extinct in the late 17th century due to hunting and invasive species.

name: Woolly Mammoth
funFact: Woolly mammoths coexisted with early humans and their remains are still found frozen in Siberian permafrost.

name: Passenger Pigeon
funFact: Passenger pigeons once numbered in the billions and their flocks would darken the sky for hours as they flew overhead.

name: Tasmanian Tiger
funFact: Despite being called a tiger, it was actually a marsupial more closely related to kangaroos than to big cats.

name: Quagga
funFact: The quagga was half-zebra, half-horse with stripes only on the front half of its body. The last one died in 1883.
